entities.summary:
Ala' al-Din al-Bukhari (born unknown, died 1437) was a prominent Hanafi jurist (faqih), Maturidi theologian, commentator of the Qur'an (mufassir), and a mystic (Sufi) who shaped Islamic scholarship in the 15th century. A prolific scholar and polymath, al-Bukhari's works influenced scholars across the Islamic world, from the Middle East to North Africa and the Iberian Peninsula. His commentaries on the Qur'an remain a key reference for Islamic jurisprudence to this day.


Ala' al-Din al-Bukhari's significance extends beyond his individual contributions, as his work reflects the broader cultural and intellectual currents of the medieval Islamic world. His writings demonstrate the complex interplay between theology, jurisprudence, and mysticism that characterized this period.


The legacy of al-Bukhari can be seen in the continued study and application of his commentaries, which have remained a cornerstone of Islamic scholarship for centuries. His influence extends beyond the Islamic world, as his works have inspired scholars from other traditions to engage with Islamic thought and culture.


The mystic's own journey was marked by spiritual struggles and epiphanies, as recorded in his autobiographical work, 'Riyad al-salihin'. His life and writings offer a rare glimpse into the inner workings of a medieval Islamic mystic.

Ala' al-Din al-Bukhari's impact on Islamic scholarship is undeniable, yet his influence extends beyond the realm of Islamic thought. His commentaries on the Qur'an have been studied by scholars of Jewish, Christian, and secular traditions, highlighting the shared intellectual heritage of the medieval Islamic world.


Ala' al-Din al-Bukhari's significance is not limited to his individual contributions, but also reflects the broader cultural and intellectual currents of the medieval Islamic world. His works demonstrate the complex interplay between theology, jurisprudence, and mysticism that characterized this period.
